what_was_proven: A Nemotron-H Mamba2 SSM implementation produces outputs and persistent state that match ggml's ggml_ssm_conv and ggml_ssm_scan to floating-point precision. ggml is llama.cpp's independently maintained reference, and it is linked in as a static library rather than reimplemented, so this is genuine independent parity rather than a self-comparison.

reference.note: The same finite inputs are fed to both paths from a single shared Stage object, so any difference is attributable to the arithmetic, not to differing inputs.

conv_io.note: The input and output have different layouts. ggml's sx is {d_conv-1+n_t, d_inner} while its dst is {d_inner, n_t}. Assuming both were the same was a real bug found by this test.

layouts_that_matter.B_and_C_per_group: B and C are {d_state=128, n_group=8}. Within one group there are 128 elements, not group_state=1024. Using group_state as the per-group stride caused a buffer overflow that crashed ggml, and was also caught by this test.
layouts_that_matter.dt_source: dt comes from the ssm_in projection at offset 10240, NOT from the conv output. The conv output contains only x, B and C.

results.persistent_state: Verified by splitting the sequence into two chunks and continuing each path from its OWN final state. At n_t=16 split 8+8, chunk1 y cosine 1.000000000000 rel 2.50e-07, chunk2 y cosine 1.000000000000 rel 2.70e-07, chunk2 state cosine 1.000000000000 rel 1.76e-07.

bugs_found_by_this_test: Per-group stride for B and C used group_state (1024) instead of d_state (128), overflowing the ggml tensor and crashing the process with 0xC0000005.
ssm_in projection offsets were applied to the conv output. The conv output only contains x, B and C, and dt is not part of it.
ggml conv input and output were assumed to share a layout. The input is channel-major and the output is token-major.

scope.covers: causal conv1d and selective SSM scan for one Nemotron-H SSM block, plus the grouped RMS norm, z gate and output projection in the implementation under test.
does_not_cover: Real GGUF weights. The test uses deterministic synthetic inputs; no tensor values from the model were read.
The attention and MoE blocks. This is the SSM arm only.
GPU execution. Both paths run on the CPU.
